I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole adult life. Thirty years teaches you what the ground wants and what it won't forgive. My 12 mu breaks down simply in my head: 8 mu stays in the wheat-maize rotation — that's my food security and steady income — and the other 4 mu goes to cotton for the cash. My wife and I can manage that alone.

**Wheat (8 mu, sown October):** I'll use the improved variety I've relied on the last several seasons — it handles our dry winters better than the old seed. I do rotary tillage after maize harvest because it's fast and saves my back. I split my nitrogen: base fertilizer before sowing, topdress at jointing. I irrigate four times — winter water, jointing, heading, grain fill — my well can handle it. Two pesticide passes: one herbicide in winter, one fungicide around heading for powdery mildew.

**Maize (8 mu, sown June right after wheat harvest):** I go straight in with no-tillage direct seeding — I can't afford to lose planting date waiting to prepare the field. Hybrid seed, no question, everyone uses hybrid now. Summer has some rain so I'll only irrigate twice: once before sowing if the soil is dry, once at silking if it's a hot summer. Two sprays — one for herbicide, one for pests.

**Cotton (4 mu, sown late April):** I plough this field in spring. Bt hybrid cotton — I still remember how bad bollworm was before Bt, I'm not going back. Cotton needs more attention: four irrigations, five pesticide applications. I'm not cutting corners on cotton because it's where I make most of my cash income.
